record.paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Hyperfine effects in the global phase diagram
record.original_question: What quantitatively accurate role do Ho hyperfine interactions play in the global concentration-temperature-transverse-field phase diagram of LiHoxY1−xF4, especially in regimes where the ferromagnetic or spin-glass critical temperature drops below roughly 0.5 K and the hyperfine interaction inhibits quantum fluctuations and strongly renormalizes the critical transverse field?

evidence.quote: As the critical (ferromagnetic or spin glass) temperature decreases, and drops below approximately 0.5 K, the role of the hyperfine interaction in inhibiting quantum fluctuations and strongly renormalizing the critical transverse field cannot be ignored [32, 33].

While progress has been achieved as to how to proceed [33], work does remain to be done to investigate via quantitatively accurate calculations (e.g. quantum Monte Carlo simulations) the role of hyperfine interactions on the global x − T − Bx phase diagram of LiHoxY1−xF4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the diluted dipolar quantum Ising magnet defined as follows. On a tetragonal (LiYF4-type) lattice, place Ho^{3+} ions independently at random with concentration x ∈ (0,1] at each rare-earth site, the remaining sites being occupied by non-magnetic Y^{3+}. To each Ho^{3+} site i associate (i) an effective low-energy doublet described by a Pauli operator σ_i^z (longitudinal Ising component) with transverse component σ_i^x, and (ii) a nuclear spin I_i = 7/2 coupled to the electronic moment by an on-site hyperfine interaction A_0 I_i · S_i (with S_i the full electronic angular momentum projected onto the relevant crystal-field manifold). The Ho-Ho electronic moments interact through the long-range magnetic dipolar interaction (with both longitudinal Ising couplings and off-diagonal terms generated by a transverse field). A uniform transverse magnetic field B_x is applied along a crystallographic a-axis.

The microscopic Hamiltonian thus has the schematic form
H = (1/2) Σ_{i ≠ j} ε_i ε_j [ J_{ij}^{zz} σ_i^z σ_j^z + (off-diagonal dipolar terms induced by B_x) ] − Γ(B_x) Σ_i ε_i σ_i^x + A_0 Σ_i ε_i I_i · S_i,
where ε_i ∈ {0,1} are i.i.d. Bernoulli(x) site occupations, J_{ij}^{zz} are the dipolar couplings on the LiYF4 lattice, and Γ(B_x) is the transverse-field-induced tunneling splitting computed from the full Ho^{3+} crystal-field spectrum.

Problem. Determine, by quantitatively accurate (e.g. unbiased quantum Monte Carlo) calculations, the global phase diagram of this model in the three-dimensional parameter space (x, T, B_x), with the full hyperfine term retained. In particular:
(a) Compute the boundary between the paramagnetic phase and the ordered (ferromagnetic for x close to 1, spin-glass for intermediate x) phase as a surface T_c(x, B_x).
(b) Quantify how the hyperfine interaction renormalizes the critical transverse field B_x^c(x, T) in the regime where T_c(x, B_x = 0) ≲ 0.5 K, where suppression of quantum fluctuations by the nuclear spins is non-negligible.
(c) Determine how the hyperfine coupling alters the location and nature of the quantum critical points and quantum critical lines, including any modifications to the universality class of the transitions.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works (e.g. Schechter–Stamp; Tabei et al.; quantum Monte Carlo studies of the diluted dipolar Ising model with renormalized transverse field; and more recent quantum-annealing microscopics work, ~2021) have made progress incorporating hyperfine effects, often by approximating them via a renormalization of the transverse field. However, a fully quantitative determination of the global x–T–B_x phase diagram of LiHoxY1−xF4 with the complete hyperfine structure retained—particularly the spin-glass regime and the strongly hyperfine-renormalized low-temperature quantum critical region—has not been definitively achieved, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Theory of the Magnetic phase diagram of LiHoF4
status_evidence.snippet: The phase diagram is derived as a function of transverse field, temperature, and dipole concentration; hyperfine interactions are central.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier theoretical work derived the phase diagram including hyperfine terms but treated dilution and disorder approximately.

status_evidence.title: Microscopics of Quantum Annealing in the Disordered Dipolar Ising Ferromagnet LiHoxY1−xF4
status_evidence.snippet: On-site hyperfine interaction is approximately taken into account through a renormalization of the transverse applied magnetic field.
status_evidence.claim: Recent QMC-related treatments still approximate hyperfine effects via transverse-field renormalization rather than full inclusion.

status_evidence.title: Phase diagram of diluted Ising ferromagnet LiHoxY1−xF4
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum Monte Carlo study of the diluted dipolar Ising model in a transverse field with approximations for hyperfine coupling.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitatively accurate full hyperfine treatment in the global (x,T,B_x) phase diagram has not been completed.
